title: Budgie (musician) - Wikipedia
notes: Peter Edward Clarke, born 21 August 1957; grew up in St Helens; art school in Liverpool, rehearsing at Eric's; the Spitfire Boys and Big in Japan, then the Slits' Cut (1979). Joined Siouxsie and the Banshees in September 1979 on the Join Hands tour, meant as a temporary replacement for Kenny Morris, and stayed until the split in 1996; nine studio albums. Co-founded the Creatures with Siouxsie in 1981 (drums and percussion, marimba, metallophone). Taiko duets with Leonard Eto for Hai! (2003). Later John Cale, the Indigo Girls, Juno Reactor, Efterklang, John Grant, Hercules and Love Affair, Los Angeles with Lol Tolhurst and Jacknife Lee (2023); a memoir, The Absence (2025). Legacy: NME readers' best drummer of 1983; Spin's No. 28 of the 100 greatest drummers of alternative music ('he didn't just play rhythms - he played hooks and leads ... His tom-tom-intensive approach, [was] enlightened by his awareness of world music'; Into the Light his 'most booming moment'). Stewart Copeland: 'very economical and offbeat ... a lot of tom-toms and a big throb'. Ari Up: 'He could go from reggae to punk to funk to jazz [...] but still very steady.' David Cavanagh: with Terry Chambers 'the outstanding English drummer of the post-punk era'. Ian McCulloch: Pete de Freitas 'loved [Budgie's] drumming'. Taylor Hawkins: 'the tribal thing he was doing was so innovative'. Jamie Miller of Bad Religion: his favourite drummer. Married Siouxsie in 1991; divorced 2007.

title: Siouxsie and the Banshees - Wikipedia
notes: The band, 1976-1996: Siouxsie Sioux, Steven Severin; Budgie on drums from 1979; John McGeoch guitar 1980-82; Robert Smith 1982-84; John Valentine Carruthers 1984-87.

title: Kaleidoscope (Siouxsie and the Banshees album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 1 August 1980 (Polydor), co-produced with Nigel Gray; Budgie's and John McGeoch's first album with the band; drum machines and synthesizers on some tracks (Red Light, Lunar Camel). Personnel: Budgie drums (1-5, 7-11), harmonica, bass guitar (2), percussion. On Skin he asked Gray for a second kit, 'as if I was playing to myself a call and answer'. Rick Buckler of the Jam called Happy House and Christine 'innovative'.

title: Juju (Siouxsie and the Banshees album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 19 June 1981 (Polydor), recorded at Surrey Sound with Nigel Gray co-producing; singles Spellbound and Arabian Knights; 'prominently featured the intricate percussion work of band member Budgie'. Arabian Knights began as a tune of Siouxsie's in waltz time. Personnel: Budgie drums, percussion.

title: Tinderbox (Siouxsie and the Banshees album) - Wikipedia
notes: Released 21 April 1986; sessions at Hansa in Berlin from May 1985, but Cities in Dust was recorded entirely at Matrix Studios, London, in September 1985. Jon Savage in Spin: 'Budgie's drumming is superb.' Personnel: Budgie drums, percussion; produced by the band.

title: Happy House - Wikipedia
notes: Single, 7 March 1980; the group's first record with McGeoch and Budgie. 'Budgie, who was interested in African polyrhythms, used a reggae vibe on the song.' Number 17.

title: Christine (Siouxsie and the Banshees song) - Wikipedia
notes: Single, 30 May 1980, the second from Kaleidoscope; number 22.

title: Israel (Siouxsie and the Banshees song) - Wikipedia
notes: Stand-alone single, 28 November 1980; written on the road in Europe; the first single composed with McGeoch and Budgie; co-produced by Nigel Gray, with a 30-singer Welsh choir.

title: Spellbound (Siouxsie and the Banshees song) - Wikipedia
notes: Single, 22 May 1981; co-produced with Nigel Gray; personnel: Budgie drums and percussion. Number 22.

title: Arabian Knights (song) - Wikipedia
notes: Single, 24 July 1981, the second from Juju; co-produced with Nigel Gray; number 32.

title: Dear Prudence - Wikipedia
notes: The Banshees' version: single, 1983, recorded in Stockholm in July 1983 and finished at Angel, Robert Smith on guitar in place of McGeoch; their biggest UK hit, number 3. Budgie: the band were fans of the White Album except Smith, and chose Dear Prudence because it was the one song he knew.

title: Cities in Dust - Wikipedia
notes: Single, 18 October 1985, from Tinderbox; number 21 in the UK, 17 on the US dance chart.

title: Kiss Them for Me (song) - Wikipedia
notes: Single, 1991, from Superstition; Talvin Singh on tabla. 'The song's drum beat was taken from a Roland TR-909 drum machine beat that had previously been used on Schoolly D's 1985 single P.S.K. What Does It Mean?' Why the song is not among his here.
